ideas.headline: 2026-11-09 midday: First Solar slides about 5% (about 7% worse than the S&P 500) after Piper Sandler cut its price target from $251 to $222 but kept its Buy-type (Overweight) rating; lower oil prices also weighed on energy stocks.
ideas.why_not_priced_in: The trigger is weak. One analyst trimmed his price target, kept the Buy rating, and said FSLR is 'the only scaled, fully domestic supplier' that meets the new US rules on Chinese-linked supply. The other cause is sector rotation as oil fell. Neither changes the business. The company is still very profitable (about 58% gross margin in Q3, EPS up from $4.24 to $5.30) and is buying back $500M of stock. Today's US anti-dumping duties on solar cells from India, Indonesia and Laos also help a US maker like FSLR. Earnings were October 29, so today's move is not an earnings reaction. FSLR swings a lot from day to day, trades far more than $300M a day, and is well below its highs (52-week range about $166-$321). The price held near $190-191 through midday instead of falling further. Risks: bookings have slowed and the company cut its 2026 sales forecast on October 29, so this is not a clean story, and a 20% trailing stop protects the position.
ideas.plain_reason: One analyst trimmed his target but still says buy; the business still earns big profits.

plain_summary: Stocks are down across the board after a hot inflation report. GE Vernova fell about 6% because one customer, SoftBank, scaled back some turbine plans, which looks like an overreaction, so I picked it as one buy idea. I skipped Nvidia because its CEO is under investigation.

ideas.headline: 2026-11-10 morning: GE Vernova down about 5-7% (opened -9%) after SoftBank disclosed a $3.7B charge on prepaid US data-center power equipment and revised its Piketon, Ohio project plans; Musk had claimed SoftBank was 'defaulting' on turbine orders.
ideas.why_not_priced_in: The fear is that AI data centers will cut back on power equipment, but the news is about one customer's own accounting. SoftBank lost its advance payments, and GE Vernova presumably keeps those deposits. SoftBank also says it may get up to $2.1B in rebates on future purchases, which means it plans to keep buying. Even if all 9.2 GW of the Ohio plant were GEV's, that is under a tenth of the roughly 122 GW of gas equipment GEV had under contract at the end of September. Turbines are in short supply, so freed-up slots can be resold. GEV raised its 2026 guidance on Oct 28. The stock is very volatile and already fell about 9% on Nov 4, so it is probably below its 50-day average. It is coming back from its low at the open, not still dropping.
ideas.plain_reason: One customer scaled back, but turbines are scarce and other buyers will take them.
